clue.text: Sporting groups in university coming in for a little soccer, initially

indicators.note: the university letter is said to come into the word for, so it is placed inside it

parts.note: some, as in 'have a little' or 'have some'

indicators.note: signals that only the opening letter of soccer is wanted

parts.note: first letter of soccer

explanation.surface: Teams of students at a university join in a casual kickabout of football.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is only a link; 'coming in' does the inserting.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf matches between two pairs are called foursomes, so these are groups formed for sport.

clue.text: Flounder, perhaps, in search in pursuit of accommodation

indicators.note: the search word chases the accommodation word, so it comes after it

parts.note: a flat is a place to live, a form of accommodation
to fish for something is to search for it

explanation.surface: Someone floundering while hunting for a place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flounder' looks like a verb meaning struggle; with 'perhaps' it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The flounder is an example of a bottom-dwelling fish with a flattened body, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: University on top of feasible merger

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: uni is the informal short form of university
'on' means possible or doable, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: A university considering a practical amalgamation with another institution.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a joining together of parties, the same thing as a merger or amalgamation.

clue.text: Close clever site to be revamped for regular traffic?

parts.note: to shut is to close

indicators.note: revamping remodels something, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An order to shut down a smart website so it can be redesigned.
explanation.definitionFit: A shuttle service runs vehicles back and forth on a fixed timetable, a regular flow of traffic.

clue.text: Generator of boom surrounding the French prophet

indicators.note: the boom generator goes around the French article

parts.note: Mach 1, the speed of sound, produces a sonic boom; written MACH I
la is French for the

explanation.surface: Something producing a loud boom encircles a French prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of Mach 1 is written as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Malachi is the Old Testament prophet whose book closes the Christian Old Testament.

clue.text: Failing Soho supremo?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: Soho, London's old red-light district, is a place of sin, and its ruler would be the king of sin

explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a London district long known for nightlife and vice, so its boss is a 'sin king'.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that is sinking is in decline, which is what failing means.

clue.text: Get tense reprimand

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
to wig is an old British verb meaning to scold or rebuke

explanation.surface: Become anxious and receive a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: To wig someone, meaning to scold them, survives in the word 'wigging'.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is British slang for understanding something, as 'get' means grasp the point.

clue.text: One distraught girl embraced by old politician leading to wild sequence of events

indicators.note: the inner letters are held within the politician's name

parts.note: the Whigs were a historic British party, forerunners of the Liberals
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: a distraught person is in a disordered state, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An upset young woman hugged by a former MP sets off a chaotic chain of happenings.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirligig is something that spins continually, hence a giddy round of happenings, as in Shakespeare's 'whirligig of time'.

clue.text: Thriller writer about to fill in family connection

indicators.note: the about word fills a gap within the family word

parts.note: genes are what relatives share by inheritance
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A crime novelist preparing to complete details of a relative's link.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene wrote thrillers such as Brighton Rock and The Third Man.

clue.text: Dairy product, something of high quality, taken on by type of cat?

indicators.note: the quality word is taken on behind the cat word, so it follows it

parts.note: the Cheshire Cat is the grinning cat of Alice in Wonderland
'the cheese' is old slang for the real thing, the best

explanation.surface: A fine dairy item adopted by a particular breed of cat.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying something is 'the cheese' once meant it was first-rate, which is also where 'big cheese' comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheshire is a crumbly English cheese from the county of the same name, made from cows' milk.

clue.text: Announcement of exit from excellent group of countries including Germany?

indicators.note: the excellent letters take in the German letter

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)
EU is the European Union

explanation.surface: A statement about a country leaving the European Union, Germany among its members.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French farewell, something said on leaving or saying goodbye.

clue.text: Concocted clue/hint about start of meal now?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the meal's opening letter
something concocted is cooked up, so these letters are rearranged
only the opening letter of meal is used

parts.note: first letter of meal

explanation.surface: A cooked-up crossword hint about when to begin the midday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concocted' reworks CLUEHINT into LUNCHTIE, and M goes in before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: If the hour is midday, the present moment is the time to eat, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Ardent supporter agitated to miss Queen when touring area

indicators.note: the shortened word travels round the area letter, enclosing it
the Queen letter is left out

parts.note: frantic means agitated
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A passionate fan, upset at not seeing the Queen on her local tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to miss' takes R out of FRANTIC to leave FANTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanatic is someone with excessive zeal for a cause or team, an extreme enthusiast.

clue.text: Hormone not entirely causing offence, containing no tritium

indicators.note: the tritium letter must be absent
the last letter is cut off

parts.note: insulting means giving offence
T is the chemical symbol for tritium, a hydrogen isotope

explanation.surface: A hormone said to be offensive in a minor way, free of a radioactive ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' cuts INSULTING to INSULTIN; 'containing no' then removes its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is the pancreatic hormone that regulates blood sugar.

clue.text: Bottle and bell placed beside heather, inspiring fear?

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage, as is spine (backbone)
ting is the sound of a small bell
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A bottle and a bell set next to some heather.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'bottle' means nerve or courage, as in 'lose your bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spine-tingling story thrills or frightens, sending a shiver down the back.

clue.text: Cheating behaviour surprising to umpires

indicators.note: a surprising arrangement is an unexpected one, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Players' cheating comes as a shock to the officials.
explanation.definitionFit: Imposture is deception by pretending to be someone or something else, a form of fraud.

clue.text: Unusual idea most readily disseminated?

indicators.note: unusual letters are out of their normal order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange notion that spreads more quickly than most.
explanation.definitionFit: Something atomised is broken into fine particles or spray, so it spreads easily.

clue.text: Treasure for the GI?

parts.note: the letters G and I are fragments taken from the word EIGHT, so GI is pieces of it

explanation.surface: Buried loot intended for an American soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: A GI is a US soldier, but here it is just two letters, both found in the word EIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of eight were Spanish silver dollars, the classic pirate treasure.

clue.text: Guaranteeing to oust King next?

indicators.note: ousting the king letter removes it from the word

parts.note: ensuring means guaranteeing
R is for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Making certain the king is deposed; who comes next?
explanation.definitionFit: Ensuing describes what follows on afterwards, the subsequent thing.

clue.text: Work hard with adapter of Shakespeare to depict tragic heroine

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
Elia was the pen name of Charles Lamb, who retold the plays in Tales from Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A writer adapting Shakespeare labours to portray a doomed heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophelia is Hamlet's ill-fated love, who drowns in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: A former soldier collars military leader, giving the bird

indicators.note: the soldier word grips the leader letters, enclosing them

parts.note: vet is US short for veteran
OC is Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: An old soldier grabs a general, giving him the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving the bird' looks like a rude gesture; 'giving' is the link and 'the bird' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a black-and-white wading bird with an upcurved bill.

clue.text: Facing travel document, travel document that's incomplete

parts.note: a visa allows entry to a country

indicators.note: the second document lacks its final letter

parts.note: a visa again

explanation.surface: Confronting paperwork, one entry permit after another, the second unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Vis-a-vis is French for face to face, used to mean opposite or in relation to.

clue.text: Stink about a hydrogen-nickel compound? Unsuccessful name for element

indicators.note: the stink word goes around the other letters

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: A smell surrounds a chemical compound; one proposed name for an element failed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hahnium was proposed for element 105 (and later 108), but dubnium and hassium were adopted instead.

clue.text: I think US city will provide racetrack

parts.note: IMO is text shorthand for 'in my opinion'
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Someone musing that an American city will host a racing circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Imola in Italy is a motor-racing circuit that has staged Formula One grands prix.

clue.text: Body of followers not good for politician

parts.note: a church is a body of believers
ill means bad, not good

explanation.surface: A congregation unhappy with a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill was the British Prime Minister in the Second World War.

clue.text: We backed agreements to produce Star Wars critters

indicators.note: backed means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: OKs are approvals, agreements

explanation.surface: We sanctioned deals to make creatures for a science-fiction film.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewoks are the small furry forest dwellers of Return of the Jedi.

clue.text: Row about it is recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An argument about something is remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel; it means a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row or level, as in tiers of seats rising one above another.

clue.text: London police attending good party in spooky location

indicators.note: the police word attends, standing alongside after the others

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party
the Yard is Scotland Yard, the Metropolitan Police headquarters

explanation.surface: Metropolitan officers turn up at a lively party in an eerie place.
explanation.definitionFit: A cemetery full of tombs is the classic setting for ghost stories.
